camera: 2:1 staggered XY terrain, finite 1920×1056 frame; orthographic crown study rendered in Blender before the final pine request.

requests.canopy: Paint a production game sprite sheet of TWO different full-sized mature Korean red pines for Honro, an overcast post-medieval Korean mountain ghost story. Use the attached game props as palette and species reference. Replace the tiny sparse bonsai look with the full, layered, volumetric crowns of a forest seen from a fixed high three-quarter camera, like a meticulously pre-rendered late 1990s isometric dark fantasy strategy RPG. Elevated orthographic game view, 2:1 diamond footprint. Side by side in a 2-column 1-row sheet, perfectly separated, wide transparent gutters, each ENTIRE tree root to top fully visible. LEFT a tall, stately, thick reddish twisting trunk supporting four distinct deep bottle-green cloud-like crowns, an irregular crown with a strong pyramidal main mass, cold sage highlights. RIGHT an older wind-shaped pine with thick forked trunk and multiple broad, dramatically layered asymmetrical crowns, with abundant foliage not bare arms. The crowns each read as masses in three dimensions, directional light from upper LEFT, pale left-facing needle groupings, cool dark undersides, reflected desaturated light, carved bark. Look down enough to see the tops of the foliage, also see bark and separate foreground branches and roots. Restrained fine illustrated texture, crisp silhouette and edge, limited palette of olive pine, cool charcoal-brown and subdued sage; artistic highest quality. Alpha transparent around each object, no sky, scenery, plinth, ground patch, grid, text, vignette, overview or flat logo. The cast shadow will be laid on the real terrain in the engine. Both trees equally detailed and tall; use every quadrant of their respective cells. Large painterly game-ready art, no blur, no render border.
requests.pass-structures: Game sprite asset sheet for the misty Korean forest mountain pass in the reference, premium pre-rendered isometric art; camera fixed looking down from above, classic two-to-one diamond ground axes at +26.565 and -26.565 degrees. Transparent background, four completely separate objects in a 2-by-2 atlas of equally sized cells with wide clear padding around all sides. Do not paint a ground tile or cellar. TOP LEFT: whole rustic low timber footbridge with six sturdy posts, two low side rails and a complete readable wooden plank deck, broad enough for two walkers. Its center line runs from southwest (LOWER LEFT of that cell) up to northeast (UPPER RIGHT). TOP RIGHT: a DIFFERENT equally long weathered footbridge with wooden planks, stone abutments and low side rails. Its center line runs northwest (UPPER LEFT of that cell) down to southeast (LOWER RIGHT). For both, direction is unmistakable: endpoints are diagonally displaced by about half as much vertical difference as horizontal. Give the near railing and posts a legible separation from the walk surface. BOTTOM LEFT: small abandoned traditional Korean mountain roadside shrine, exact dark grey earthen tiled gable roof, subtle curved eaves, humble closed dark wood wall with tiny red ribbon, rough granite diamond foundation, camera reveals two adjacent wall faces and tiled roof top with one wall much more shaded. BOTTOM RIGHT: a crumbling Korean stone gateway with weathered two timber uprights, stepped granite and grey-brown lintel on a diagonal beam, rugged weathered corners. Use ONE consistent physically coherent upper-left cool directional light, muted wood/lichen/slate colors and finely painted ambient occlusion. Monument, gate and bridges share the SAME isometric camera and not frontal illustrations. All four objects fully in their own cell, no overlapping gutters, no white outlines, no character, lettering, background or watermark. A little dark underside and moss is good. No long cast shadow on the transparent empty background.
requests.pass-surfaces: Generate a 2-by-2 material atlas, equal four texture quadrants that meet exactly at the middle, NO gutters, frames, grid, text or vignettes. Premium hand-painted material textures for an original muted, dark Korean mountain pass game, viewed straight down for game texture mapping. Each of the FOUR materials is evenly lit, continuous all the way to all four boundaries of its square and detailed at gameplay size, seamless-style with no identifiable tile repeats. TOP LEFT forest ground: a varied dark pine-green moss carpet with very fine tawny needle litter, sparse tiny leaves, and a little grey soil showing, not stand-up bushes. TOP RIGHT ancient narrow trail surface: muted khaki grey ochre, compressed earth, small weathered slate gravel, scattered roots and weathering, no trail silhouette or edges. BOTTOM LEFT deep flowing mountain stream: cool blue-green translucent river water, irregular soft directional current and glints, blue-black pools, scattered fine muted turquoise caustic lines, no shore, no large white waves. BOTTOM RIGHT gravel in shallow water at natural bank: rounded river stones and grit, dark wet / dry grey-brown and moss desaturated sage, tiny submerged pebbles, occasional small glint, pristine unbroken texture. Cared-for late 1990s dark fantasy isometric RPG painterly realism with tactile texture, unified overcast late-afternoon ambience. Textures should be atmospheric and readable, not abstract noise or shiny digital filters. Four large distinct material close-ups ONLY.

pineCorrection: Paint finished, richly textured in-game sprites directly over the two orthographic 3D tree blockouts in the FIRST reference. LOCK that exact elevated camera, approximate exterior silhouettes and occlusion of the roots. The second reference is ONLY an example of the project's architectural camera and palette. Two old full-size Korean pines for a dark Korean mountain forest, separate 2-column single row atlas, transparent background. We are looking DOWN ONTO the tree crowns like Diablo II or a classic high-angle isometric strategy game; foliage faces are seen predominantly from ABOVE. Critically, at least 84% of the projected vertical silhouette must be foliage or branches with pine needles. Roots should be a short glimpse of trunk through lower-front foliage; never expose a bare trunk the length of a human. Irregular 3-D mounds of blue-green needles fill the silhouette that the gray blockout specifies, all around a central crown. The front canopy genuinely occludes the trunk, rear lobes visible above it. Replace polygons with very detailed, finely layered pine boughs and needle fans. TREE A taller loosely conical Korean evergreen with a slight lean and dark inner spaces between front and back groups. TREE B ancient, broader, wind-shaped canopy with a forked branch briefly seen through the needles and a few warmer brown needle clusters. Slightly different silhouettes but SAME elevated camera and scale. Natural asymmetric forests, no geometric facets, no cones of smooth plastic, no bonsai terraces, no sparse side-profile tree, no flat disks seen edge on. Restrained dark cedar green, cool blue-grey in the shadow, muted warmer sage highlights from upper-left, bark warm rust. Cast shadows on the ground will be generated from these exact silhouettes by the game. Alpha transparent outside both separated cutouts, generous center gutter. No floor, no pedestal, no reference grid or lettering, no sky. Keep each crown completely inside its own half. Style: meticulous pre-rendered painterly dark-fantasy game sprites, readable light/dark around the volume, tactile needle detail.
